usa.fact: The United States declared its independence from Britain on July 4, 1776, which Americans celebrate as Independence Day.
usa.ask: Which country declared its independence from Britain on July 4, 1776?

usa.fact: In 1969 astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin of the United States became the first people to walk on the Moon.
usa.ask: Which country's astronauts were the first people to walk on the Moon, in 1969?

canada.fact: L'Anse aux Meadows in Newfoundland, Canada, is the only known Viking settlement in North America, from about 1,000 years ago.
canada.ask: Which country's L'Anse aux Meadows is the only known Viking settlement in North America?

canada.fact: Canada celebrates Canada Day on July 1, the day in 1867 when it became a country.
canada.ask: Which country celebrates its birthday on July 1, marking its founding in 1867?

canada.fact: Basketball was invented in 1891 by James Naismith, a teacher born in Canada.
canada.ask: Which country was James Naismith born in, the teacher who invented basketball in 1891?

mexico.fact: Teotihuacan, in Mexico, was one of the largest cities in the world about 1,500 years ago and is home to the giant Pyramid of the Sun.
mexico.ask: Which country's ancient city of Teotihuacan has the giant Pyramid of the Sun?

mexico.fact: Mexico's capital, Mexico City, was built on top of Tenochtitlan, the Aztec capital that stood on an island in a lake.

mexico.fact: At the Maya city of Chichén Itzá in Mexico, the shadow of a snake seems to slither down the El Castillo pyramid at the spring and fall equinoxes.

guatemala.fact: El Mirador, in Guatemala's rainforest, was a huge Maya city more than 2,000 years ago, with La Danta, one of the largest pyramids in the world.

belize.fact: Belize was called British Honduras until 1973 and became independent in 1981.
belize.ask: Which country was called British Honduras until 1973?

belize.fact: Caracol, in Belize, was a huge Maya city. Its Caana pyramid is still one of the tallest buildings in Belize.
belize.ask: Which country's ancient Maya city of Caracol has a pyramid still among the tallest buildings there?

el-salvador.fact: Joya de Cerén, in El Salvador, is a Maya farming village that was buried by volcanic ash about 1,400 years ago and is called the "Pompeii of the Americas."
el-salvador.ask: Which country's Joya de Cerén is a Maya village buried by volcanic ash, the "Pompeii of the Americas"?

nicaragua.fact: The ruins of León Viejo in Nicaragua are one of the oldest Spanish colonial towns in the Americas, founded in 1524.

costa-rica.fact: Costa Rica got rid of its army in 1948.
costa-rica.ask: Which country got rid of its army in 1948?

costa-rica.fact: In Costa Rica's Diquís Delta, people carved hundreds of nearly perfect stone spheres more than 1,000 years ago.
costa-rica.ask: Which country's Diquís Delta has hundreds of nearly perfect stone balls carved long ago?

panama.fact: In 1513 Vasco Núñez de Balboa crossed the land of Panama and became the first European to see the Pacific Ocean from the Americas.
panama.ask: Across which country did Balboa hike in 1513 to become the first European to see the Pacific from the Americas?

bahamas.fact: Christopher Columbus first landed in the Americas in October 1492 on an island in the Bahamas that the Lucayan people called Guanahani.

jamaica.fact: Port Royal in Jamaica, once a famous pirate town, partly sank into the sea during an earthquake in 1692.
jamaica.ask: Which country's old pirate town of Port Royal partly sank into the sea in a 1692 earthquake?

haiti.fact: Haiti became independent on January 1, 1804, after a revolution led by formerly enslaved people, making it the first Black-led republic.

haiti.fact: The Citadelle Laferrière, a huge mountaintop fortress in Haiti, was built in the early 1800s after independence.
haiti.ask: Which country's Citadelle Laferrière is a huge mountaintop fortress built in the early 1800s?

dominican-republic.fact: Santo Domingo, the capital of the Dominican Republic, founded in 1496, is the oldest city still lived in that Europeans founded in the Americas.
dominican-republic.ask: Which country's capital, founded in 1496, is the oldest European-founded city in the Americas still lived in?

antigua-and-barbuda.fact: Nelson's Dockyard in Antigua and Barbuda is a British navy dockyard from the 1700s, named after Admiral Horatio Nelson.
antigua-and-barbuda.ask: Which country's Nelson's Dockyard is an 18th-century British navy base named after Admiral Nelson?

dominica.fact: Christopher Columbus named Dominica in 1493 after the day he saw it, a Sunday, called domingo in Spanish.
dominica.ask: Which island country did Columbus name in 1493 after the day of the week he spotted it, a Sunday?

saint-lucia.fact: The small island of Saint Lucia is the birthplace of two Nobel Prize winners: economist Arthur Lewis and poet Derek Walcott.
saint-lucia.ask: Which small island country is the birthplace of Nobel Prize winners Arthur Lewis and Derek Walcott?

barbados.fact: Barbados became a republic in 2021, replacing the British queen as its head of state.
barbados.ask: Which island country became a republic in 2021, replacing the British queen as head of state?

barbados.fact: In 1751 a young George Washington visited Barbados, the only trip outside mainland North America he ever made.
barbados.ask: Which island country did a young George Washington visit in 1751, his only trip abroad?

brazil.fact: Brazil, once a colony of Portugal, declared its independence on September 7, 1822.
brazil.ask: Which South American country, once ruled by Portugal, declared independence on September 7, 1822?

brazil.fact: The giant Christ the Redeemer statue looking over Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, was finished in 1931.
brazil.ask: Which country's giant Christ the Redeemer statue, finished in 1931, looks over Rio de Janeiro?

brazil.fact: Brazil built a brand-new capital city, Brasília, in the middle of the country and moved its government there in 1960.
brazil.ask: Which country built a brand-new capital in the middle of the land and moved there in 1960?

argentina.fact: The Cave of the Hands in Argentina has hundreds of hand outlines painted on the rock, the oldest more than 9,000 years ago.
argentina.ask: Which country's Cave of the Hands has hundreds of hand outlines, the oldest painted over 9,000 years ago?

argentina.fact: Argentina declared its independence from Spain on July 9, 1816.
argentina.ask: Which country declared independence from Spain on July 9, 1816?

chile.fact: The Chinchorro people of northern Chile began making mummies about 7,000 years ago, some of the oldest known mummies in the world.

peru.fact: Caral, in Peru, is about 5,000 years old and is one of the oldest known cities in the Americas.

peru.fact: Cusco, high in the Andes of Peru, was the capital of the Inca Empire.
peru.ask: Which country's mountain city of Cusco was the capital of the Inca Empire?

bolivia.fact: Tiwanaku, near Lake Titicaca in Bolivia, was the center of a great empire more than 1,000 years ago and has the carved Gateway of the Sun.

bolivia.fact: Cerro Rico, a mountain above the city of Potosí in Bolivia, gave the Spanish Empire huge amounts of silver starting in the 1540s.
bolivia.ask: Which country's Cerro Rico mountain at Potosí gave the Spanish Empire huge amounts of silver?

colombia.fact: Ciudad Perdida, the "Lost City" in Colombia's mountains, was built around the year 800, about 650 years before Machu Picchu.
colombia.ask: Which country's Ciudad Perdida, the "Lost City," was built about 650 years before Machu Picchu?

colombia.fact: Lake Guatavita in Colombia inspired the legend of El Dorado, about a Muisca chief covered in gold dust who offered gold to the lake.
colombia.ask: Which country's Lake Guatavita inspired the legend of El Dorado, the man of gold?

ecuador.fact: In 1978 Quito, the capital of Ecuador, was one of the very first places named a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
ecuador.ask: Which country's capital was one of the first places named a UNESCO World Heritage Site, in 1978?

venezuela.fact: Simón Bolívar, called "the Liberator" for leading much of South America to independence from Spain, was born in Caracas, Venezuela, in 1783.

suriname.fact: In a 1667 peace treaty, the Dutch kept Suriname while the English kept New Netherland, which became New York.

paraguay.fact: In Paraguay, the mission towns of La Santísima Trinidad de Paraná and Jesús de Tavarangue were built by Jesuits and Guaraní people in the 1700s.

trinidad-and-tobago.fact: Christopher Columbus named the island of Trinidad, now part of Trinidad and Tobago, in 1498, after the Holy Trinity, when he saw three peaks on the land.

uruguay.fact: Uruguay's football team won the Olympic gold medal in both 1924 and 1928.

saint-kitts-and-nevis.fact: Brimstone Hill Fortress in Saint Kitts and Nevis, a well-kept British fortress on a steep hill, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
